solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Medicine's short — not a good time for hajj

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medicine
a time that is not good is a grim age

explanation.surface: A pilgrim complains that the medical supplies have run low during the trip to Mecca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medicine's short' reads as a complaint, but it is PIL, a pill missing its last letter; 'not a good time for' then suggests GRIM AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The hajj is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca, an example of a sacred journey.

clue.text: Raised a drink, something taken at restaurant in Nice

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: to lap is to drink, as a cat does
diners take a table at a restaurant

explanation.surface: Toasting with a glass while dining in the French city of Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French Riviera city; it is the adjective, pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatable means pleasant to taste or acceptable, much like nice.

clue.text: What first-class fare gets the foreign newly-wed

parts.note: le is French for the
a groom is a man just married

explanation.surface: Asking what a foreign groom is served in first class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like food; here it is a passenger paying a fare.
explanation.definitionFit: First-class passengers enjoy generous space for stretching their legs.

clue.text: Stylish Hilary for one maintains business link?

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: maintains means the term holds and keeps the business inside it

parts.note: Hilary is one of the terms of the Oxford academic year
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A fashionable woman called Hilary keeps a business connection going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hilary' looks like a person; it is the Oxford University spring term.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom is a communication system linking rooms in a building.

clue.text: Current tributes inspiring small hospital's skills

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the tributes take those letters inside

parts.note: compliments are tributes of praise
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Recent praise for a small hospital's abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective, recent; it is electrical current.
explanation.definitionFit: Accomplishments are skills or achievements acquired by effort.

clue.text: Perhaps a grey English fruit lacks carbon

indicators.note: lacks means the fruit is missing the named element

parts.note: a quince is a hard pear-shaped fruit
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A dull English fruit low in carbon content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grey' reads as a colour; a grey is a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey is a horse with a white or grey coat, so it belongs to the horse family.

clue.text: Tribal group determined to seize power

indicators.note: to seize means the first word grabs and holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: set, as in set on doing something, means determined
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A clan resolved to take over the reins of government.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a clan or branch of a family, especially in Ireland or Scotland.

clue.text: Dean's works are so absurdly racialist

indicators.note: absurdly means in a ridiculous way, so the letters are jumbled nonsensically

explanation.surface: A complaint that a dean's writings are ludicrously bigoted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dean is Jonathan Swift, Dean of St Patrick's in Dublin, author of Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's books are famous examples of biting satire.

clue.text: Sprain muscle going about tango opener

indicators.note: going about means the words wrap around the letter for tango

parts.note: to pull a muscle is to strain or sprain it
abs are stomach muscles; AB is one
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pulling a muscle while dancing the opening steps of a tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tango opener' reads as the start of a dance; tango only gives T, and opener is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring pull on a drinks can is lifted to open it.

clue.text: Organisational reason to take one's temperature

indicators.note: to take means the first word swallows the following pieces within it

parts.note: logic is reasoning
one is I, and 's is the short form of is

explanation.surface: A sensible explanation for checking your own fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Logistic describes the planning and coordination of supplies, people and operations.

clue.text: Squadron, say, drops one veteran without number

indicators.note: drops means the letter for one falls out of the word

parts.note: a squadron is an example of a military unit
I is the Roman numeral one
a veteran is old

explanation.surface: An air force squadron loses one of its old hands, and is left without enough men.
explanation.definitionFit: Untold means too many to be counted, countless or innumerable.

clue.text: Second person no longer still ignores Grand Hotel

indicators.note: ignores means those letters are left out of the word

parts.note: though and still both mean nevertheless
G is grand and H is hotel, as abbreviations

explanation.surface: A runner-up who no longer stays at the Grand Hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second person' sounds like the runner-up in a race; it is grammar, the archaic singular you.
explanation.definitionFit: Thou is the old second-person singular pronoun, now obsolete in ordinary speech.

clue.text: Pay corps to recruit a foreign judge

indicators.note: to recruit means the corps takes the new member in among its letters

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
un is French for a
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A Pay Corps hires a judge from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay corps' suggests the army pay corps; Pay is the definition, and the corps is REME, the army engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To remunerate is to reward someone with money for work done.

clue.text: Fool bishop with pre-noon tipple, swigging litres

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a.m. means before noon

indicators.note: swigging means the drink takes the letter for litres inside it

parts.note: booze is alcoholic drink, a tipple

explanation.surface: A clergyman is fooled by a morning drink that knocks back litres.
explanation.definitionFit: To bamboozle is to trick or deceive someone.

clue.text: Notice Yankee attack butter

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice or poster
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to go at is to attack

explanation.surface: A poster in the US urges an assault on dairy produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' reads as the dairy spread; it is one who butts with its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Male goats are well known for charging and butting with their horns.

clue.text: South Island's diving aid

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
Cuba is an island; 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A southern island's main attraction is its diving gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuba is the self-contained underwater breathing apparatus used by divers.

clue.text: Dislike a pint drunk at Hackney Arms

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are befuddled into a new order
arms are the limbs at each side, so the outside letters of the word

parts.note: first and last letters of Hackney

explanation.surface: Disliking a pint downed at a pub called the Hackney Arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hackney Arms' looks like a pub name; Arms picks the outer letters of Hackney, a district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipathy is a strong feeling of aversion or hostility.

clue.text: Vestry typically holds object of worship husband left

indicators.note: holds means the first word contains the second within it

parts.note: say means for example, typically

indicators.note: left means the husband has gone away, out of the word

parts.note: Christ is worshipped by Christians

explanation.surface: A church vestry typically contains a sacred object left behind by a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristy is the room in a church where vestments and sacred vessels are kept.

clue.text: Celebrate former superior officer

parts.note: ex means former
U means upper class, socially superior
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A one-time senior officer is commemorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior officer' reads as one rank above; it splits into U, upper-class, and LT, lieutenant.
explanation.definitionFit: To exult is to rejoice triumphantly.

clue.text: Kiss player possessing fine special quality

indicators.note: possessing means the words hold the letter for fine inside them

parts.note: X is the sign for a kiss
an actor is a player on stage
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A kissing scene by an actor with a fine and special presence.
explanation.walkthrough: The X Factor was a British TV talent show, and the phrase means an elusive star quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an indefinable quality that makes someone stand out.

clue.text: Like good guy arresting city mugger

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: arresting means the good guy holds the city inside him

parts.note: a saint is a good person
LA, Los Angeles, is a city

explanation.surface: Like a hero detaining a street robber in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is an attacker; a mugger is one who attacks and robs.

clue.text: Evergreen duchess's elegance pointed up somewhat

indicators.note: in a down clue, pointed up means the letters run upwards, backwards
somewhat means only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: A duchess's grace is enhanced and endures through time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointed up' sounds like emphasised; here it turns the letters bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen describes something that never seems to get old, timeless.

clue.text: Current going round Circle Line track

indicators.note: going round means the current surrounds the two letters after it

parts.note: a flow is a current
O is the shape of a circle

explanation.surface: An electric current circling London's Circle Line tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle Line track' reads as the London Underground line; Circle is O and Line is L.
explanation.definitionFit: To track someone is to follow or trail them.

clue.text: Spoil bouncer, one in his 70s?

parts.note: to baby someone is to spoil or pamper them
a boomer is a large male kangaroo, which bounces

explanation.surface: Pampering a nightclub doorman who is getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman; it is a kangaroo, called a boomer in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby boomers were born in the post-war birth surge, so around the time of the puzzle they were in their seventies.

clue.text: Keen lapwing drops it, heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means running right to left, backwards
drops means those letters fall out of the bird's name

parts.note: peewit is another name for the lapwing, from its call

explanation.surface: An eager bird lets something fall as it flies west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager; it is the verb, to wail in grief.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in mourning, so it means to cry or lament.

clue.text: Second fee securing Republican's easy victory

indicators.note: securing means the fee holds the letter firmly inside it

parts.note: a toll is a fee for passage
R stands for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican wins comfortably after a second round of fundraising.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a walk-over, a contest won without effort.

clue.text: Ignorant individual blocks new reduced trail

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the word new taken as written

indicators.note: blocks means the letter for an individual sits in the way, inside the trail

parts.note: a scent is a trail followed by a hound
I is a single individual, one

explanation.surface: One person obstructs a shortened new hiking trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescient is a rare literary word for lacking knowledge, from Latin nescire, not to know.

clue.text: Commie wrong to have moved to the left

indicators.text: to have moved to the left
indicators.note: a letter of the word is taken out and placed one spot further left

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A communist is mistaken for having shifted politically leftward.
explanation.walkthrough: In TORT the R shifts one place left, ahead of the O. The political left in the surface is just a direction in the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trot is a slang name for a Trotskyist, a type of hard-left communist.

clue.text: Panto dame's son and why his ways are deviant

indicators.note: deviant means straying from the norm, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: Questioning why a pantomime character behaves so oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: Wishee Washee is the son of Widow Twankey, the dame in the pantomime Aladdin; a panto is a British Christmas stage show for families.
explanation.definitionFit: The panto character's name is spelt Wishee Washee, which sounds just like this word for feeble or insipid.
